bluf: JumpFly is a Hoffman Estates, IL paid media specialist for SMB advertisers, a Google Premier Partner since 2003 managing paid search, paid social, Amazon and marketplace ads, SEO and email. It now sells ChatGPT Advertising and Predictive AI Audiences, practising what it sells on search: 359 own Google ads, 236 in the last 30 days, and 23 LinkedIn ads. The record shows no pricing model, no social pixel on its own site and a 13 client book that is all case studies. The one thing a rival should know: Horus places it most exposed to the platforms absorbing the execution layer, the very hours it sells.
doing:
The positioning line reads: Google Premier Partner online ad agency managing paid search, paid social, Amazon and marketplace ads, SEO and email for 20+ years. In plain words, a PPC shop for small and mid sized advertisers trading on the Google badge and longevity. The headline claim is trust: Google Premier Partner and trusted partner since 2003, with 150+ client reviews on Clutch and Google.

The sold mix leads with Paid Search at score 3: PPC leads the title, the Premier Partner badge sits on the homepage, the Transparency Center holds 359 own ad creatives and the site carries dozens of PPC case studies. Paid Social, Retail Media and SEO score 2 at core: a Paid Social Media page with Meta cases (Dana-co, Mulberry Market Designs, Whistling Kettle); Amazon Ads & Marketplaces with ads pitching Amazon, Walmart and Wayfair management; SEO in the homepage title with cases for The Stationery Studio, MyPlace Self-Storage and Power Planter. Five lines score 1 (AI automation, AI search, CRO, email, programmatic); B2B, content, creator, data, local and web score 0; breadth 9. The one proprietary item is Predictive AI Audiences; the one partner is Google Premier Partner.

AI posture: it sells ChatGPT Advertising and Predictive AI Audiences and pitches its Google ads work as strategy driven by AI plus human expertise; a LinkedIn ad asks whether the brand is in the answer when customers ask ChatGPT.

Dated moves: the record holds one, undated, the launch of ChatGPT Advertising services, with no release date on the pages read. Activity shows elsewhere: case studies dated through 2026-09-03 and blog posts dated 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-25 on AI Max, entity SEO and holiday search planning. No news items, no jobs and no ATS are in the record.

Pricing signals are absent. For a 20+ year paid media specialist the record also shows no employee count, no ownership, no data and measurement line and no creative or web line.
clients:
The client type on record is SMB, across ecommerce, healthcare, industrial and B2B, HVAC, business services and travel; the home market is the US from Hoffman Estates, IL.

The record names 13 clients: 13 observed and 0 names only, all from case studies or case slugs, none shared with another tracked agency. One row, PPC and, is a title fragment, not a client. Wedding Linens Direct (2026-09-03) came for paid and social, paid ad management credited with increased online revenue; Dana-co (2026-07-09) for paid, social and brand, a scalable paid media strategy across three brand portfolios; The Stationery Studio for paid (automated daily budget rules, 2026-07-08) and SEO (2026-04-13); Carolina Vasectomy Reversal (2026-03-30) for leads and paid through call quality scoring; Phoenix Phase Converters (2025-08-05) for paid, monthly revenue records from call tracking data; American Chairs (2025-11-04) for paid, organic and web, revenue up 81% year over year. MyPlace Self-Storage (2026-07-08) came for organic demand, organic clicks up 59.3% year over year. Unique Truck Equipment (2025-10-22) came for commerce on Amazon.

The observed mix is paid performance (share 0.591), organic demand (0.096) and social and creators (0.086). These are SMB advertisers whose execution hours KJ4 (The platforms are absorbing the execution layer) says the platforms are taking, so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that they ask next for first party data, creative volume and measurement, none of which the record shows as a line here.

openings:
The strongest opening is price against automation. JumpFly sells the paid search and paid social execution hours that KJ4 says the platforms are absorbing, to an SMB book the Monsoon read scores at displacement 62.1 with automation overlapping 36% of the movable hours: a rival that prices on outcomes, since the record lists no pricing model (P5 unknown), and shows first party data and measurement depth is likely, with moderate confidence, to undercut it. The falsifier: a published pricing model or a case study showing measurement or incrementality work.

The contradiction to lead with is paid social: it sells the line and runs no social ad pixel on its own site. The gap to lead with is proof on AI ads: it sells ChatGPT Advertising with no holdout or incrementality capability in the record (P8 partial) and no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial), so the first rival to show a holdout tested ChatGPT ads result sets the price.

Contestable clients are the paid performance rows, ecommerce and industrial SMBs such as American Chairs, Phoenix Phase Converters and Battery Mart; every one is a public case study, so the pitch against it can quote its own numbers.
